In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a framework that allows for a fair, automated and objective evaluation of algorithms for automatic lesion segmentation in stroke patients.
the automatic segmentation of ischemic stroke lesions from multi-spectral magnetic resonance imaging data.
the evaluation of algorithms for the automatic segmentation of ischemic stroke lesions from MR images.

the state of the art is not good enough yet to be used in a clinical setting for the segmentation of acute or subacute stroke lesions.
no algorithmic characteristic was found to perform better than the others.

we have proposed an open evaluation framework, created multi center, multi modality and multi protocol databases, organized a challenge with 14+7 participating groups, and released the results and the databases.

the ISLES challenge was the first step towards a standardized evaluation of algorithms for ischemic stroke lesions.

the current state of automated lesion segmentation algorithms is not yet mature.
